docs.title: Django Model Versions
docs.text: Simple, efficient and intuitive version control for your Django models.

docs.title: Why Django Model Versions?
docs.text:
Tracking changes in your database shouldn't be a headache. You need a solution that is:

  • Zero Config: Just add a mixin and you're done.
  • Ultra Efficient: Optimized queries and bulk operations support.
  • Flexible: Automatic by default, but fully controllable when you need it.
  • Developer Friendly: Type-hinted, intuitive API (as_of, between).

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Automatic Versioning: Saves a copy of your model on every save and delete.
  • Efficient Querying: Time travel made easy with as_of, between, latest, and earliest.
  • Manual Control: Opt-out of automatic versioning and use context managers for specific updates.
  • Bulk Operations: Create history for thousands of records in a single query.
  • Admin Integration: Built-in support for viewing history in Django Admin.

docs.title: Manual Control
docs.text: Sometimes you don't want to save every single keystroke. We give you full control.

docs.title: Disable Automatic Versioning
docs.text:
Set VERSIONING_AUTO = False on your model to disable automatic versioning on save/delete.

class DraftPost(VersionableMixin, models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=100)

    # Disable auto-versioning for this model
    VERSIONING_AUTO = False

docs.title: Force Versioning on Demand
docs.text:
Use the force_versioning context manager to create a version explicitly, even if VERSIONING_AUTO is False.

from django_model_snapshots import force_versioning

post = DraftPost.objects.create(title="Draft") # No version created

# Make a major change and record it
with force_versioning():
    post.title = "Published"
    post.save() # Version created!

docs.title: Bulk Operations
docs.text:
Creating thousands of records? Don't kill your database with N+1 inserts. Use bulk_create_history.

from django_model_snapshots import bulk_create_history

products = [Product(name=f"Product {i}") for i in range(1000)]

# 1. Bulk create the main objects
Product.objects.bulk_create(products)

# 2. Bulk create their history (1 query!)
bulk_create_history(products)

docs.title: Field Selection
docs.text:
By default, all fields are versioned. To save space, specify only what you need using versioning_fields.

class UserProfile(VersionableMixin, models.Model):
    bio = models.TextField()
    last_login = models.DateTimeField() # We might not want to version this

    # Only version the bio
    versioning_fields = ["bio"]

docs.title: VersionableMixin
docs.text:
django_model_snapshots.mixins.VersionableMixin

Mixin to add versioning capabilities to a Django model.

Attributes:

  • VERSIONING_AUTO (bool): If True (default), creates a version on every save() and delete().
  • versioning_fields (list[str], optional): List of field names to include in the history. If None (default), all fields are included.

Properties:

  • history: Returns a HistoryQuerySet filtered for the current instance.

docs.title: HistoryQuerySet
docs.text:
django_model_snapshots.managers.HistoryQuerySet

Custom QuerySet for historical models.

Methods:

docs.title: as_of(date: datetime) -> Optional[Model]
docs.text: Returns the version of the object as it existed at the given date. Returns None if the object did not exist.

docs.title: between(start: datetime, end: datetime) -> QuerySet
docs.text: Returns a QuerySet of versions that existed between the given start and end dates.

docs.title: latest() -> Optional[Model]
docs.text: Returns the most recent historical record.

docs.title: earliest() -> Optional[Model]
docs.text: Returns the oldest historical record.

docs.title: force_versioning
docs.text:
django_model_snapshots.context.force_versioning

Context manager to force versioning creation within a block, overriding VERSIONING_AUTO=False.

with force_versioning():
    obj.save()

docs.title: bulk_create_history
docs.text:
django_model_snapshots.utils.bulk_create_history

Signature: bulk_create_history(objs: List[Model], history_type: str = "+") -> None

Efficiently creates history records for a list of objects in a single query.

  • objs: List of model instances (must be of the same class).
  • history_type: The type of history record ('+' for created, '~' for changed, '-' for deleted). Defaults to '+'.

docs.title: VersionAdmin
docs.text:
django_model_snapshots.admin.VersionAdmin

ModelAdmin subclass that adds a "History" button to the change view and renders a history list page.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the package using pip:

pip install django-model-versions

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Add django_model_snapshots to your INSTALLED_APPS in settings.py:

settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    ...
    'django_model_snapshots',
    ...
]

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Inherit from VersionableMixin in your model. That's it!

models.py
from django.db import models
from django_model_snapshots import VersionableMixin

class Product(VersionableMixin, models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    price = models.DecimalField(max_digits=10, decimal_places=2)

Now, every time you save() or delete() a Product, a historical record is created automatically.

# Create a product (Version 1 created)
product = Product.objects.create(name="Laptop", price=1000)

# Update it (Version 2 created)
product.price = 900
product.save()

# Delete it (Version 3 created - deletion marker)
product.delete()

docs.title: Accessing History
docs.text:
Every versioned object gets a .history property. It returns a HistoryQuerySet filtered for that object.

product = Product.objects.get(id=1)

# Get all versions
all_versions = product.history.all()

docs.title: Efficient Querying (Time Travel)
docs.text: Stop writing complex date filters. Use our intuitive API.

docs.title: as_of(date)
docs.text:
Get the version of the object as it existed at a specific time.

from django.utils import timezone
from datetime import timedelta

yesterday = timezone.now() - timedelta(days=1)
old_version = product.history.as_of(yesterday)

docs.title: between(start, end)
docs.text:
Get all versions created within a time range.

start = timezone.now() - timedelta(weeks=1)
end = timezone.now()
changes = product.history.between(start, end)

docs.title: latest()
docs.text:
Efficiently retrieve the most recent historical record.

latest_version = product.history.latest()

docs.title: earliest()
docs.text:
Efficiently retrieve the oldest historical record.

original_version = product.history.earliest()

docs.title: Admin Integration
docs.text:
To view history in the Django Admin, inherit from VersionAdmin.

admin.py
from django.contrib import admin
from django_model_snapshots import VersionAdmin
from .models import Product

@admin.register(Product)
class ProductAdmin(VersionAdmin):
    list_display = ("name", "price")

This adds a History button to the change view of your model, allowing you to see a list of all historical changes.
